1: The church of God which is at Rome to the church of God which is at Corinth, and to all who in every place are called by the will of God through our Lord Jesus Christ: Grace and peace be multiplied to you by Almighty God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

Let us set before our eyes the noble examples of our own generation. Because of envy and jealousy the greatest and most righteous pillars of the church were persecuted and contended unto death. Let us set before our eyes the good apostles: Peter, who endured not one or two but many labours; and Paul, who taught righteousness to the whole world and reached the farthest limits of the West.

Let us then approach Him in holiness of soul, lifting up pure and undefiled hands to Him, loving our gracious and merciful Father who made us a part of His elect. For thus says the scripture: When the holy number of the righteous is increased, then will I come to you — and the number is not yet full, and the door is not yet shut.
2: Consider the heavens, how they move by His ordering and without discord; consider the sun and the moon and the stars, how they follow their course without swerving; consider the seasons, how they give way to one another in peace; consider the seas, how they do not transgress their bounds. All these He has established in harmony, and His harmony is the pattern of our peace.
[1 Clement 20:11-12 — The order of the lowly]

The small and the great are equal in the sight of the order of God: the ox and the lion, the cedar and the hyssop, the king and the beggar — each has its place in the harmony, and the harmony is not broken by the lowliness of any part, but by the pride of any part.

Let our whole body be preserved whole in Christ; let each of us be subject to his neighbour, according to the special grace given to him. Let the strong care for the weak, and the weak respect the strong; let the rich supply the needs of the poor, and the poor give thanks that they have a helper.
3: For who is there among you who has not tasted of the grace of the Spirit? The one gift does not belittle the other: the ear and the eye serve one body, and the foot and the head serve one body, and the body is not ashamed of its foot, nor the foot of its dust.

Let him who has love in Christ keep the commandments of Christ. Who can describe the bond of the love of God? What man is able to tell the excellence of its beauty, as it deserves to be told? The height to which love exalts is unspeakable. Love unites us to God; love covers a multitude of sins; love endures all things, is long-suffering in all things. Without love, nothing is pleasing to God.

See that you do not deprive yourselves of the good things that are to come. For it is written: Eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has it entered into the heart of man what He has prepared for those who wait for Him. Let us then, beloved, be found among the number of those who wait, that we may receive the promise — for the promise is not small, and the waiting is not long, and the One who promised is faithful.
